# Plotting references

`minimal.json` is a newly written synthetic plotting projection. `default.png`
renders it with zero-value options; `crop.png` renders frame 1 with title
`Inclusive crop` and `PeakMaxSCLLuminance`. Go 1.27.1 windows/amd64 and
`golang.org/x/image v0.46.0` produced these manually inspected baselines. Tests
compare decoded RGBA pixels, including an opaque canvas, rather than PNG bytes.
They are not regenerated by tests.

`numeric-reference.json` was generated by `oracle.rs`, calling the pinned Rust
library's actual estimators and including its `src/utils.rs` transfer functions.
The oracle's aggregation matches `draw_brightness_series` in `src/commands/plot.rs`.
No Go implementation is involved in expected-value generation.

Upstream: quietvoid/hdr10plus_tool revision
`82cb01ba387184476dbf5fa3bddebf0a345693d7` (tool 1.7.2, library 2.1.5), MIT
licensed; see the retained third-party notice. Toolchain: `rustc 1.95.0
(59807616e 2026-04-14)`. The oracle uses serde_json 1.0.151. Ordinary Go tests do
not require Rust, upstream assets, or network access.

The real-input assets under upstream `assets/hevc_tests` are used locally and
not redistributed here. Original SHA-256 values:

| File | Frames/profile/scenes | SHA-256 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| regular_metadata.json | 259 / A / 3 | 3F4844B02D8A6DCCDB769FA296854B1CA7FC5FF45E885C320BFBADCFBD1652FC |
| single-frame-metadata.json | 1 / B / 1 | 1232027CA68B9F97B2D770F798A4C29B5C9F3006D7C7E1699890F035E391FFC7 |
| metadata-dhdr10-opt.json | 30 / A / 6 | 264B837E42D0C3405D357166E3CCA66A88B9B41767EAB812BCE8BD05AE027124 |

To reproduce the numerical oracle in a temporary directory, create this Cargo
manifest, substituting your pinned upstream and library checkout paths:

```toml
[package]
name = "hdr10plus_plot_oracle"
version = "0.0.0"
edition = "2024"

[dependencies]
hdr10plus = { path = "C:/path/to/hdr10plus_tool/hdr10plus", features = ["json"] }
serde_json = "=1.0.151"

[[bin]]
name = "oracle"
path = "E:/github/go-hdr10-plus/testdata/oracle.rs"
```

The actual generation command used these paths:

```powershell
$taskOutput = Join-Path $env:TEMP 'hdr10plus-implementation-20261008'
$env:HDR10PLUS_REFERENCE = 'C:/Users/Audionut/AppData/Local/Temp/hdr10plus-plot-plan-source-20261008'
cargo run --release --manifest-path (Join-Path $taskOutput 'oracle\Cargo.toml') -- (Join-Path $taskOutput 'regular_metadata.json') (Join-Path $taskOutput 'single-frame-metadata.json') (Join-Path $taskOutput 'metadata-dhdr10-opt.json') 1> 'E:\github\go-hdr10-plus\testdata\numeric-reference.json' 2> (Join-Path $taskOutput 'oracle-build.log')
```

Go comparisons use absolute PQ tolerance `1e-12` and nit tolerance
`max(1e-6, 1e-9*abs(reference))`. These pass for all fixed y ticks, zero,
representative HDR values, uint32 maximum, all four estimators, constant and
varying synthetic samples, all three real inputs, and their crops. No widening
of the planned tolerance was needed.

Run the optional real-input differential check:

```powershell
$env:HDR10PLUS_REFERENCE_DIR = 'C:\path\to\hdr10plus_tool\assets\hevc_tests'
go test -run '^TestUpstreamDifferential$' -v .
```

Rust image references were built locally with:

```powershell
cargo build --release --no-default-features --features internal-font --manifest-path 'C:\Users\Audionut\AppData\Local\Temp\hdr10plus-plot-plan-source-20261008\Cargo.toml'
```

`hdr10plus_tool.exe plot -i regular_metadata.json -p SOURCE -o rust-SOURCE.png`
generated the four source references. The crop reference also supplied `-s 1
-e 1 -t 'Inclusive crop'` with max-scl-luminance. Go renders were generated from
a separate temporary importing module with a local replace directive. Inspect
the envelopes, tick scale, series order and legend values, allowing the documented
font, tick and text placement differences. Rust images and its bundled font are
not redistributed in this repository.

To intentionally update the Go goldens, render `minimal.json` through the public
API with the options specified above, encode with `image/png`, inspect both
images, and then replace the corresponding files. Investigate unexplained
pixel differences before updating a baseline.
